name: Lizard Mountain
generated_description:
Lizard Mountain rises to 4,803 feet in Texas. The Lizard Mountain Trail covers 0.9 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 16 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 30.35786, -103.71332 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 190 miles southeast of El Paso, Texas. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

October through April is the comfortable window here — summer temperatures at this elevation are dangerously hot, so if you must hike in summer, start at first light and carry more water than you think you need.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
